title: feat(core): compute `toModelOutput` before `tool-result` chunk emission and forward `providerMetadata` through harness
body:
## Summary

Two related changes that together let harness consumers (such as the mastracode TUI) read a tool's `toModelOutput` result without re-running the tool:

1. **Compute `toModelOutput` before emitting the streaming `tool-result` chunk.** Previously it was only computed *after* the chunk was already on the wire, when updating the message list. This meant the streaming chunk never carried `mastra.modelOutput` — only the persisted message did.
2. **Forward `providerMetadata` through the harness `tool_end` event and `tool_result` content** (both streaming and history replay), so consumers can read it directly off the harness surface.

## What changes

### Core behavior change: hoist `getProviderMetadataWithModelOutput`

`packages/core/src/loop/workflows/agentic-execution/llm-mapping-step.ts`

- Compute `getProviderMetadataWithModelOutput(toolCall)` **before** the streaming `tool-result` chunk is emitted, then thread the merged metadata into `chunk.payload.providerMetadata`.
- The same value is reused when updating the message list, so it's computed once per tool call (previously the hoist would have doubled the work; now it's deduplicated).
- Both the "successful-results-on-error-turn" path and the main `inputData` loop are updated.
- `providerExecuted` tools are skipped (matches the pre-existing message-list path behavior).

### Harness plumbing

`packages/core/src/harness/types.ts`

- Add optional `providerMetadata?: Record<string, unknown>` to the `tool_end` event and to the `tool_result` content variant on harness messages.

`packages/core/src/harness/harness.ts`

- Streaming path: when consuming a `tool-result` chunk, forward `payload.providerMetadata` on the pushed `tool_result` content part and the emitted `tool_end` event.
- History replay (`convertToHarnessMessage`): pass `part.providerMetadata` through for both `tool-invocation` (state `'result'`) and `tool-result` parts so reloaded threads carry the same data.

`modelOutput` already lives at `providerMetadata.mastra.modelOutput` — the same location `message-list.ts`'s `storedModelOutputs` reads from. Forwarding `providerMetadata` directly avoids creating a second source of truth and lets consumers read any future `mastra.*` fields without another core change.

## Why

Tools can already produce structured `toModelOutput` content (e.g. `{ type: 'content', value: [{ type: 'media', mediaType: 'image/png', data: '<base64>' }] }`). That content already reaches the model (PR #16449 normalizes it for AI SDK providers), but harness consumers never saw it on the streaming path — they only got the raw `result` value. With the hoist + harness forwarding, harness UIs can read `providerMetadata.mastra.modelOutput` and render the same multi-modal output the model sees, in real time.

## Test plan

- New assertion in `llm-mapping-step.test.ts`: after `toModelOutput` runs, `controller.enqueue` is called with a `tool-result` chunk whose `payload.providerMetadata.mastra.modelOutput` equals the `toModelOutput` return value.
- `pnpm --filter ./packages/core test -- --run llm-mapping-step harness` — 271/271 pass.
- `pnpm --filter ./packages/core check` — clean.

## Risk

Low. The behavior change is additive:

- The hoist moves a computation earlier in the same function — its output is now reused instead of recomputed. Tools without `toModelOutput` are unaffected (the helper returns `undefined` and the chunk falls back to the original `providerMetadata`).
- `providerMetadata` is only added as an optional field on the harness `tool_end` event and `tool_result` content variant.
- Existing message-list update logic for `toModelOutput` is preserved.

title: fix(core): preserve message-level providerOptions across tool-call turns
body:
## Description

Fixes the `UIMessage → ModelMessage` conversion in `@mastra/core` so message-level `providerOptions` (e.g. Anthropic's `cacheControl: { type: 'ephemeral' }`) survive through to the LLM call when the conversation history contains tool calls. Previously the conversion mapped messages by array index, but an assistant turn with a tool call splits into `[assistant, tool]` model messages, breaking the alignment for every message after it — so the marker landed on the wrong message or vanished, blocking the rolling prompt-cache breakpoint pattern for tool-using agents.

- Replaced the batch-convert + `result.map((_, i) => preprocessed[i])` index lookup in `aiV5UIMessagesToAIV5ModelMessages` with per-UI-message conversion that attaches metadata to the produced model message of matching role.
- Added a regression test covering the issue scenario: `[user, assistant-with-tool-call, user-with-cacheControl]` — verifies the marker lands on the trailing user model message and not on the tool-result message.
- Added a second regression test covering message-level `providerOptions` on an assistant tool-call turn — verifies it stays on the assistant model message and is not migrated to the tool-result message on roundtrip.
- Verified end-to-end against the live Anthropic API: captured outgoing HTTP body confirms `cache_control` reaches the API on the correct content part after the fix; on pre-fix code it landed on the `tool_result` part.

title: fix(core): normalize `toModelOutput` media types for AI SDK provider compatibility
body:
## Summary

Fixes tools with `toModelOutput` that return image content (like screenshot tools) not being visible to the model.

## Problem

`toModelOutput` returns `{ type: 'media', mediaType: 'image/png', data: ... }` which matches the `@ai-sdk/provider` TypeScript types (`LanguageModelV2ToolResultOutput`). However, AI SDK providers at runtime expect `type: 'image-data'` — and silently drop any unrecognized content part type.

AI SDK normally normalizes `media` → `image-data` internally in `mapToolResultOutput`, but Mastra calls `toModelOutput` directly via `getProviderMetadataWithModelOutput` and stores the result in `providerMetadata.mastra.modelOutput`, bypassing that normalization step.

### Affected providers

| Provider | `type: 'image-data'` (normalized) | `type: 'media'` (unnormalized) |
|---|---|---|
| **Anthropic** | Native `image` block | Silently dropped |
| **Google/Gemini** | `inlineData` | Silently dropped |
| **OpenAI (Responses API)** | `input_image` with data URI | Dropped + warning |
| **OpenAI (Chat Completions)** | `input_image` with data URI | Dropped + warning |
| **OpenAI-compatible** | `JSON.stringify` (no image support) | Same — no difference |

Any tool using `toModelOutput` to return image/file content was affected across all major providers.

## Fix

Add `normalizeModelOutput()` in `llm-mapping-step.ts` that runs immediately after `tool.toModelOutput()` and converts:
- `type: 'media'` with image MIME → `type: 'image-data'`
- `type: 'media'` with non-image MIME → `type: 'file-data'`

This mirrors the same mapping AI SDK does in its `mapToolResultOutput` function.

## Test Plan

- Existing `llm-mapping-step.test.ts` tests pass (26/26)
- Typecheck clean
- Manually verified: screenshot tool images now visible to Claude models via Anthropic provider

## Overview

Fixes a compatibility bug where tool results returned by toModelOutput() using Mastra's internal media shape (e.g., { type: 'media', mediaType: 'image/png', data: ... }) were not recognized by AI SDK providers and were silently dropped. The PR normalizes tool outputs immediately after toModelOutput() so they match provider-expected types (image-data/file-data), preserving media parts across Anthropic, Google/Gemini, OpenAI (Responses/Chat), and OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Description

Anthropic returns `400 unexpected tool_use_id` when recalled history contains an incomplete `tool_use` / `tool_result` pair. This commonly hits agents that use parallel tool calls and got interrupted before every tool finished — the broken pair stays in the database and crashes future turns when recall pulls it back in.

**Fix:** a pairing sanitizer that drops orphan tool blocks before the request leaves for the LLM.

### What changed

- New `sanitizeOrphanedToolPairs` in `provider-compat.ts`. Drops unpaired `tool_use` / `tool_result`; preserves valid pairs, deferred provider-executed tools, and inline server tool results.
- Wired into `aiV5UIMessagesToAIV5ModelMessages`, gated on `filterIncompleteToolCalls` so only the LLM-submission path runs it. Inspection paths are untouched.
- 13 unit tests + verified end-to-end against the live Anthropic API: 8 orphan scenarios all returned `400` before the sanitizer and `200 stop_reason=end_turn` after.

## ELI5

When an AI agent recalls old conversations, it sometimes picks up incomplete tool instructions (like a "request to do X" without a "result of doing X", or vice versa). The AI provider (Anthropic) refuses these incomplete pairs and returns an error. This PR adds a cleanup function that removes these orphaned pieces before sending the message, so the AI doesn't reject it.

---

## Overview

Fixes Anthropic API `400 unexpected tool_use_id` errors that occur when semantic recall assembles messages containing orphaned `tool_use` or `tool_result` blocks. This commonly happens when agents run parallel tool calls and runs are interrupted, leaving incomplete tool-invocation pairs in the message history.

**Solution:** Implements `sanitizeOrphanedToolPairs()` — a utility function that removes unpaired tool-invocation parts before LLM submission while preserving valid tool pairs, provider-executed tools, and inline server-side tool results.

## Implementation Details

**New Function: `sanitizeOrphanedToolPairs`** (70 lines in `provider-compat.ts`)
- Filters message content arrays to remove mismatched `tool-call`/`tool-result` blocks

title: fix: support old core worker lifecycle

This keeps the node deployer compatible with projects that are running a newer deployer/CLI against an older `@mastra/core`.

Before, the server always called the new worker lifecycle API:

```ts

```

Now it prefers the new API, but falls back to the old event engine API when `startWorkers` is not available:

```ts
if (typeof workerLifecycle.startWorkers === 'function') {
  await workerLifecycle.startWorkers();
} else {

}
```

title: fix(playground): forward client headers on auth actions
body:
Closes #15470

Studio's `makeSSOLoginRequest` and `makeLogoutRequest` were calling `fetch` with only `Content-Type`, silently dropping any custom headers configured in Studio settings. This broke prod setups behind tenant middleware or composite auth that require a header (e.g. `x-tenant-id`, `Authorization`) on `/auth/sso/login`.

Now spreads `client.options.headers` into both calls, matching the pattern already used in `use-auth-capabilities`. `Content-Type` is placed after the spread so user headers can't accidentally override it.

Before:
```ts
await fetch(url, {
  credentials: 'include',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
});
```

After:
```ts
const { headers: clientHeaders = {} } = client.options || {};
await fetch(url, {
  credentials: 'include',
  headers: { ...clientHeaders, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
});
```

Added unit tests covering header forwarding for both `makeSSOLoginRequest` and `makeLogoutRequest`. Same defensive `Content-Type` ordering applied to `use-auth-capabilities` for consistency.

title: feat(cli): add `mastra verify` command for pre-deploy validation
body:
## Summary

Adds a standalone `mastra verify` command that validates a Mastra project is ready to deploy — without uploading anything.

It runs the same preflight checks as `mastra studio deploy` and `mastra server deploy` (missing env vars, host-local storage paths) and exits with a status code reflecting whether the project would be accepted by the platform.

## Why

Today, the only way to surface preflight issues is to start a real deploy. That's slow (build + zip + upload + platform poll), hits the platform API unnecessarily, and isn't usable from CI without auth credentials.

`mastra verify` gives projects a fast, credential-free way to:

- Gate PRs (`mastra verify --strict` as a GitHub Action step)
- Catch regressions locally before pushing (pre-commit hook, `pnpm verify` script)
- Iterate on preflight rules without burning deploy attempts

## Usage

```bash
# build + validate
mastra verify

# skip build, validate existing .mastra/output
mastra verify --skip-build

# validate against a specific env file
mastra verify --env-file .env.production

# treat warnings as errors (CI mode)
mastra verify --strict

# JSON output (for CI tooling)
mastra verify --json
```

Exit codes:
- `0` — preflight passed (no issues, or warnings only)
- `1` — at least one error-severity issue, or any issue in `--strict` mode

## Test plan

- 7 new unit tests in `verify-project.test.ts` covering: pass with no issues, pass with warnings, exit 1 on error, exit 1 in strict mode, JSON output (ok), JSON output (blocked), JSON output (no env file).
- Verified full preflight suite still passes (66 tests across deploy-preflight, studio/deploy, server/deploy, verify).
- Typecheck clean for changed files.
- Lint clean for changed files.

## Notes

The preflight module was added in #16317. This PR is purely a new entry point — no behavior change to existing deploy commands.

## Description

Adds the `agents` storage domain to `@mastra/mssql`, bringing it to parity with `@mastra/mongodb` and `@mastra/libsql` for that domain. `MSSQLStore.stores` now includes `agents` alongside the existing five domains (`memory`, `workflows`, `scores`, `observability`, `backgroundTasks`).

Without this domain, any code path that calls `mastra.getEditor().listResolved()`, the Studio "Agents" tab, or AB-style agent-builder tools throws `Agents storage domain is not available` when MSSQL is configured as storage. This is a pure feature gap — no changes are required to `@mastra/core` or any other adapter.

### Implementation

- New module `stores/mssql/src/storage/domains/agents/index.ts` defining `AgentsMSSQL extends AgentsStorage`. Implements all 13 abstract methods (entity CRUD + version CRUD), `init`, `dangerouslyClearAll`. `listKey` and `versionMetadataFields` come from the abstract base — not redeclared, matching the pattern in `@mastra/mongodb` and `@mastra/libsql`.
- Tables `mastra_agents` and `mastra_agent_versions` created from the shared `AGENTS_SCHEMA` / `AGENT_VERSIONS_SCHEMA` constants in `@mastra/core/storage` — no schema duplicated.
- Three default indexes mirroring mongo's strategy:
  - `mastra_agents (createdAt DESC)` — accelerates the default `list()` order.
  - `mastra_agent_versions (agentId, versionNumber DESC)` UNIQUE — version uniqueness + accelerates `getLatestVersion`.
  - `mastra_agent_versions (agentId, createdAt DESC)` — `listVersions` default order.
- All errors wrapped in `MastraError` with `createStorageErrorId('MSSQL', ...)` op IDs mirroring the LibSQL adapter (`GET_AGENT_BY_ID`, `CREATE_VERSION`, `DELETE_VERSIONS_BY_AGENT_ID`, etc.).
- Pagination uses T-SQL `OFFSET … ROWS FETCH NEXT … ROWS ONLY` (with required `ORDER BY`). Metadata filtering uses `JSON_VALUE([metadata], '$.key')`. Identifiers bracket-quoted; parameters `@named`.
- No legacy-schema migration: this is the first version of the `agents` domain on the MSSQL adapter.

### Tests

The generic agents test suite from `stores/_test-utils/src/domains/agents` runs automatically because `MSSQLStore.stores.agents` is now populated. All ~20 cases pass against the docker-compose SQL Server container, including: create/getById round-trip + auto-creation of version 1, `getByIdResolved` falling back to latest version when no `activeVersionId`, update merging metadata, delete cascading to versions, list pagination + ordering + `perPage: false`, concurrent metadata updates.

Outside this PR's scope.

The other ten missing domains on the MSSQL adapter (`promptBlocks`, `scorerDefinitions`, `mcpClients`, `mcpServers`, `workspaces`, `skills`, `blobs`, `datasets`, `experiments`, `schedules`) are deliberately left for follow-up PRs to keep this one focused, reviewable, and easy to merge.

title: Skip applied ALTERs in ClickHouse init to prevent replica races
body:
## Description

Fixed intermittent agent hangs when ClickHouse observability storage was configured. On Replicated/Shared MergeTree tables, every `ALTER` statement bumps the table's metadata version even when the change is a no-op (e.g., `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` on an existing column). Re-issuing these statements on every process boot caused replica catch-up races, leading to "metadata version on replica is N, while common metadata is N+1" errors. When init failed, the storage proxy cached the rejected promise, causing all subsequent storage calls to hang.

**Changes:**
- Refactored `ALL_MIGRATIONS` from raw SQL strings to structured `MigrationEntry` objects with `kind`, `table`, `name`, and `sql` fields
- Added helper functions `addColumn()` and `addBloomIndex()` to generate migration entries
- Refactored `buildRetentionDDL()` → `buildRetentionEntries()` to return structured `RetentionEntry` objects instead of raw SQL
- Added `parseTtlExpression()` to extract column and days from ClickHouse TTL expressions (handles both input and normalized forms)
- Added `filterAppliedMigrations()` to introspect `system.columns` and `system.data_skipping_indices` and skip migrations whose target already exists
- Added `filterAppliedRetention()` to introspect `system.tables.create_table_query` and skip `MODIFY TTL` statements that wouldn't change the current TTL
- Updated init logic to call these filter functions before executing ALTERs, reducing metadata churn to zero on steady-state databases
- Falls back to running all statements if introspection fails (preserves correctness on older ClickHouse versions or restricted-permission users)

This PR prevents intermittent agent hangs during ClickHouse observability storage initialization by introspecting ClickHouse system metadata and skipping no-op ALTER statements that would otherwise increment table metadata versions on Replicated/SharedMergeTree tables.

Problem
- Re-applying ALTERs such as ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, ADD INDEX IF NOT EXISTS, and MODIFY TTL at process boot still increments metadata versions even when the change is a no-op. This can produce replica "metadata version" mismatch errors, cause init to fail, cache rejected promises in the storage proxy, and lead to hung storage calls.

Solution
- Replace raw SQL migration list with structured MigrationEntry objects (kind, table, name, sql) and add helpers addColumn() and addBloomIndex() to generate them.
- Refactor retention DDL generation to buildRetentionEntries() returning RetentionEntry objects (table, column, days, sql) and keep buildRetentionDDL() delegating to .map(e => e.sql).
- Implement parseTtlExpression() to extract { column, days } from ClickHouse TTL expressions; it handles both input forms (INTERVAL N DAY) and ClickHouse-normalized forms (toIntervalDay(N)), and now accepts backtick-quoted identifiers (e.g., `endedAt`) so parsing succeeds when create_table_query emits quoted columns.
- Add filterAppliedMigrations() to query system.columns and system.data_skipping_indices and skip migrations whose target columns or skipping indices already exist.
- Add filterAppliedRetention() to inspect system.tables.create_table_query and skip MODIFY TTL statements that would not change the current TTL.
- Update init logic to run these filters before executing ALTERs; if introspection fails (older ClickHouse or restricted permissions), fall back to executing all statements to preserve correctness.
- Tests: unit tests for parseTtlExpression and buildRetentionEntries; integration tests verifying init idempotence (zero ALTERs on re-run), selective MODIFY TTL behavior, and re-applying migrations when columns are manually dropped.
- Changelog: .changeset entry describing the fix and release notes.

- Eliminates unnecessary ALTERs on steady-state databases, reducing metadata churn to zero in typical cases, avoiding replica races and startup hangs while preserving correctness when introspection is unavailable.

body:
Fixes #16046.

Before, a compact AI SDK v6 message with only a dynamic-tool part could normalize into an empty DB parts array, so retry, resume, approval, or regenerate flows could lose valid tool state.

After, MessageList routes dynamic-tool UI messages through the v6 adapter and preserves input-streaming, input-available, output-available, output-error, and mixed data-* parts during DB normalization.

Example after:

```ts
new MessageList().add([
  {
    id: 'assistant-plain-dynamic-tool',
    role: 'assistant',
    parts: [{ type: 'dynamic-tool', toolName: 'search', toolCallId: 'call-1', state: 'input-available', input: { query: 'weather' } }],
  },
], 'memory').get.all.db()[0]?.content.parts
```

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## ELI5

When you chat with an AI that uses tools, sometimes the conversation gets saved to a database. This PR fixes a bug where the database was losing important information about which tools were being used—like forgetting which tool was being called or what its status was. The fix makes sure that when these tool messages are saved, all the important details are kept safe so you can retry, resume, or continue the conversation without losing context.

## Overview

This PR addresses issue #16046, where MessageList was dropping plain AI SDK v6 dynamic-tool UI parts during conversion to Mastra database format. Previously, assistant messages containing only a dynamic-tool part would normalize into an empty DB parts array, causing retry/resume/approval/regenerate flows to lose valid tool state. The fix ensures these messages are properly routed through the v6 adapter and all tool state information is preserved during normalization.

## Changes by Component

### TypeDetector.ts
Added `dynamic-tool` as a definitive AIV6-only characteristic. Previously, messages containing only dynamic-tool parts were not identified as v6-only and were routed through the v5 adapter, which filtered out the tool parts. Now the detector explicitly returns `true` when encountering a `dynamic-tool` part, ensuring correct classification.

### AIV6Adapter.ts
Refactored tool UI-part conversion in `fromUIMessage` to:
- Route all tool UI parts through a dedicated `createToolInvocationPartFromUIPart` function
- Explicitly remap v6 tool states: `input-streaming` → `partial-call`, `input-available` → `call`, `output-available` → `result`, `output-error` → `output-error`
- Preserve `rawInput` and `input` fields during conversion
- Add tool result normalization via `normalizeToolResult` to unwrap `{ value }` outputs before storing as `result`
- Populate the legacy `content.toolInvocations` field by deriving it from produced `tool-invocation` parts
- Remove the previous v6-only tool-state filtering logic that depended on `isV6OnlyToolState`

### Tests
Added five new regression test cases in message-list-v6.test.ts:
- `input-streaming` state → `tool-invocation` with `state: 'partial-call'`
- `input-available` state → `state: 'call'` with inclusion in `content.toolInvocations`
- `output-available` state → `state: 'result'` with output mapped to result field
- `output-error` state → `state: 'output-error'` with errorText/rawInput preserved
- Mixed dynamic-tool and custom data parts → tool-invocation parts for tools, non-tool parts preserved in order

Added `.changeset/few-chefs-grin.md` documenting a patch-level fix for @mastra/core, noting that MessageList now preserves tool state during history normalization.

MessageList.add of an assistant message with a dynamic-tool part now produces a DB content.parts entry preserving toolName, toolCallId, normalized state, and input/output data, enabling proper continuation of tool-related conversation flows.

title: Wire role-permissions and star routes through the shared adapter test harness
body:
## Summary

Four `SERVER_ROUTES` entries were already registered by every server adapter (express, fastify, hono, koa, nestjs) via the generic `SERVER_ROUTES` iteration, but were short-circuiting in the shared adapter integration suite before any assertion ran. The routes themselves never needed adapter-specific wiring — the gaps were entirely in `server-adapters/_test-utils/`.

Affected routes:
- `GET /auth/roles/:roleId/permissions`
- `PUT /stored/agents/:storedAgentId/star` and `DELETE` sibling
- `PUT /stored/skills/:storedSkillId/star` and `DELETE` sibling

## Root causes

1. **`:roleId` had no default valid path-param mapping** in `route-test-utils.ts`, so the URL builder left the literal `:roleId` segment and every adapter answered 404.
2. **The mocked editor did not enable the `stars` builder feature**, so `requireBuilderFeature(mastra, 'stars')` threw `HTTPException(404)` for all four star routes.
3. **`GET /auth/roles/:roleId/permissions` requires an authenticated admin caller** (via `MASTRA_USER_PERMISSIONS_KEY` in `requestContext`) **plus an RBAC provider** with `getPermissionsForRole`. Neither is set up — and `MASTRA_USER_PERMISSIONS_KEY` is in `RESERVED_CONTEXT_KEYS`, so it cannot be supplied by request body/query. The harness has no clean way to seed it.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `server-adapters/_test-utils/src/route-test-utils.ts` | Map `:roleId` → `'test-role'`. |
| `server-adapters/_test-utils/src/test-helpers.ts` | Editor mock now exposes `hasEnabledBuilderConfig: () => true` and `resolveBuilder` returning `getFeatures: () => ({ agent: { stars: true } })`. Minimal feature surface — only `stars` is enabled. |
| `server-adapters/_test-utils/src/route-adapter-test-suite.ts` | Add `/auth/roles/:roleId/permissions` to `authRoutesRequiringProviders` with a comment. 200/403/404 coverage already lives in `packages/server/src/server/handlers/auth.test.ts`. |

## Test plan

- CI exercises express/fastify/hono/koa/nestjs adapter suites via `SERVER_ROUTES` iteration.
- Each of the four star routes should now hit the storage-backed handler (`agentStore.getById('test-stored-agent')` / `skillStore.getById('test-stored-skill')` — both seeded in `createDefaultTestContext`) and return `< 400`.
- `GET /auth/roles/:roleId/permissions` is intentionally skipped by the generic happy-path suite (admin + RBAC required); existing unit tests cover the per-status behavior.

## Notes

- No production code changes.
- No `@mastra/core` import additions, so `check:core-imports` is not required.
- No permission edits, so `generate:permissions` / `check:permissions` are not required.

title: fix(libsql): prevent safeStringify from dropping shared object references
body:
Workflow runs were being persisted without their top-level `result` field because libsql's `safeStringify` was treating shared (non-circular) object references as cycles.

The cycle-detection used a single `WeakSet` that was added to but never cleared, so any object that appeared more than once in the graph got dropped. In workflow snapshots, `snapshot.result` and `context[step].output` are the same reference on success, so `snapshot.result` was being silently stripped on every persist.

This broke `listWorkflowRuns` (snapshots came back with `result: undefined`) and workflow resume.

Before:
```ts
const seen = new WeakSet();
const sanitize = (val) => {
  if (seen.has(val)) return undefined; // dropped on second visit
  seen.add(val);
  // ...recurse...
};
```

After:
```ts
const ancestors = new Set();
const sanitize = (val) => {
  if (ancestors.has(val)) return undefined; // only true cycles
  ancestors.add(val);
  try { /* ...recurse... */ } finally { ancestors.delete(val); }
};
```

Regression from #12573.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## ELI5

A serializer was mistakenly throwing away shared toys when it saw the same object twice. The fix makes it only remove objects that actually form a loop, so shared objects are kept and workflow snapshots no longer lose data.

## Changes

### Fix: correct circular-reference detection in safeStringify
- File: stores/libsql/src/storage/db/utils.ts
- Replaced a global WeakSet that tracked every visited object with a per-call ancestor Set that tracks only objects on the current recursion path. Values are added on entry and removed on exit (try/finally), so only true cycles are detected.
- Result: shared (non-circular) object references are no longer treated as cycles and are preserved during serialization. This fixes a regression where snapshot.result was being stripped when it referenced the same object as context[step].output.

### Tests added
- File: stores/libsql/src/storage/db/safe-stringify.test.ts
  - New unit tests for safeStringify covering: true cycles, functions, symbols, BigInt, toJSON, throwing getters/Proxy behavior, arrays, undefined input, and importantly shared-but-non-circular reference preservation and regression cases.
- File: stores/libsql/src/storage/domains/workflows/index.test.ts
  - Regression test using an in-memory LibSQL instance verifying that persisting/loading workflow snapshots preserves the shared reference between snapshot.result and context[step].output across loadWorkflowSnapshot, getWorkflowRunById, and listWorkflowRuns.

### Changeset

## Description

Fixes a bug in `persistStepUpdate` where `requestContext` was incorrectly serialized when the `RequestContext` instance came from a different module boundary (e.g. cross-package imports in the monorepo).

This check fails when the `RequestContext` class is imported from a built package artifact vs a source-relative import (different class references). title: fix(fastify): clean up streams on disconnect
body:
This fixes Fastify stream cleanup when a client disconnects before a built-in streamed response finishes.

Before this change, the adapter only canceled hijacked streams from `reply.raw.close`. Bun can miss that response close event, so long-running streams could keep producing chunks after the client was gone. The route `abortSignal` also only watched the request side, which meant upstream work could keep running when the response closed early.

I also added focused coverage for aborted request closes, response closes, normal completed POST body closes, real Fastify client cancellation, and datastream cleanup.

title: fix(core): fix message part ordering in buildMessagesFromChunks to use first-delta position
body:
## Problem

`buildMessagesFromChunks` emitted text and reasoning parts at `*-end` time, not when they first appeared in the stream. When spans overlapped with tool calls (e.g. `text-start` → `tool-call` → `text-end`), the tool call would appear before the text part in the final message — breaking step-start insertion logic and agent loop behavior.

## Solution

Refactored part emission to use **first-delta ordering**: parts are pushed into the `parts` array when their first delta arrives (not on `*-start` or `*-end`), then mutated in-place as subsequent deltas arrive. This preserves the true stream order without accumulating deltas into intermediate arrays.

Key changes:

- **First-delta positioning** — a part is created and pushed to the array on the first `text-delta` or `reasoning-delta`, establishing its position relative to tool calls and other parts
- **In-place mutation** — subsequent deltas append directly to the part via a reference map (`textRefs`/`reasoningRefs`), avoiding `deltas[]` accumulation and `join("")` at the end
- **Metadata maps** — `*-start` chunks only stash `providerMetadata` in lightweight maps (`textMeta`/`reasoningMeta`); no part is created until content actually arrives
- **Redacted reasoning** — still pushed immediately on `reasoning-start` since redacted spans have no deltas
- **Empty reasoning** — emitted on `reasoning-end` if no deltas arrived, preserving OpenAI `item_reference` requirements (#9005)
- **Empty text cleanup** — text parts where every delta was an empty string `''` are filtered out at the end

## Testing

- Added regression test for interleaved `text-start` → `reasoning-start` → `reasoning-delta` → `text-delta` ordering (from #15914)
- Updated existing interleaved text/tool-call test to verify first-delta ordering
- All 29 tests pass

title: ci(e2e): treat cancelled jobs as failures in PR status reporter
body:
## Description

Fix the `E2E Tests` PR status check getting stuck at `pending` indefinitely when a child job hits its `timeout-minutes` cap.

### Why

`.github/workflows/secrets.e2e.yml` has two aggregator jobs that translate the matrix of e2e jobs into a single PR commit status:

- `e2e-success` fires when every `needs.<job>.result == 'success'` → posts `success`
- `e2e-failure` fires when any `needs.<job>.result == 'failure'` → posts `failure`

When a job hits its `timeout-minutes` cap, GHA force-cancels it and the result becomes `'cancelled'`, not `'failure'`. That value satisfies neither aggregator's `if:`, so both get `skipped` and the PR's `E2E Tests` status check stays at the initial `pending` (`Checking for changes`) set by `check-changes` — forever, on every PR with a timed-out shard. This is what's been happening to recent PRs whose `e2e-kitchen-sink` shard 2 hits the 15-min cap (e.g. #16242, #16241, #16239, #16237, #16234) — the failures are real, but the PR shows a green-by-default-or-stuck-pending status instead of red.

### What

- Extend `e2e-failure`'s `if:` so a child result of either `'failure'` or `'cancelled'` triggers it. Uses `contains(fromJSON('["failure", "cancelled"]'), needs.X.result)` per child to keep the expression readable.
- Guard the whole condition with `!cancelled()` so user-initiated workflow cancels — including `cancel-in-progress: true` from the workflow's own concurrency group when a new commit is pushed — don't post a false failure on the previous SHA.

No other behavior changes:
- All-success runs still post `success` via `e2e-success` (unchanged).
- Real test failures still post `failure` (unchanged).
- A genuinely user/concurrency-cancelled run posts nothing (unchanged), which is correct because the next run's `check-changes` will reset `E2E Tests` back to `pending`.
- Matrix jobs (`e2e-kitchen-sink`) report the most-severe outcome of any shard as their aggregate `needs.<job>.result`, so a single timed-out shard is enough to flip the aggregate to `cancelled` and trigger the new path.

title: fix(core): restore correct per-mode model when reopening a thread
body:
## Description

Fixes a bug in mastracode where the wrong model would be applied to the saved mode after exiting and reopening (reported in Slack: build-mode model leaking into `plan` / `fast` modes on restart).

### Root cause

`Harness.switchMode` only persists `modeModelId_<previousMode>` (the outgoing mode's model) plus `currentModeId`. When the user enters a new mode and just uses that mode's `defaultModelId` without an explicit `/model` switch, `modeModelId_<newMode>` is never written to thread metadata.

Then `loadThreadMetadata` on restart did:

1. Resolve `modeModelId_<harness default mode>` (e.g. `modeModelId_build`) into `updates.currentModelId`.
2. Restore the saved `currentModeId` (e.g. `fast`) and try to overwrite `updates.currentModelId` with `modeModelId_fast`.
3. If `modeModelId_fast` was missing (the common case above), the build model from step 1 leaked through and was applied to `fast`.

### Fix

`loadThreadMetadata` now restores the saved mode **first**, then resolves `currentModelId` for the now-restored mode using a proper fallback chain: per-mode thread metadata → mode's `defaultModelId` → legacy global `currentModelId`. The `mode_changed` event's `previousModeId` is now the actual previous mode in the harness rather than always the configured default mode (these are equivalent in practice but slightly more correct).

### Tests

Added `packages/core/src/harness/mode-model-persistence.test.ts` covering:

- saved non-default mode restores its `defaultModelId` when no per-mode override was persisted (the reported bug — fails before this change, passes after);
- explicit per-mode model is restored on reopen;
- default mode + custom model is restored on reopen;
- `mode_changed` is emitted with the correct `previousModeId` when restoring a mode.

title: docs(mcp): document custom fetch auth failure handling
body:
Adds a recipe to the `MCPClient` reference for handling auth failures inside a custom `fetch`.

Throwing from a custom `fetch` when an auth token isn't available can trigger an indefinite ~1Hz retry loop on the SDK's background GET SSE "standalone listener" stream. The MCP Streamable HTTP spec defines `405 Method Not Allowed` as the way a server signals it doesn't offer that stream, and the SDK honors it as a terminal status — so returning a synthetic 405 `Response` disables the listener cleanly when your server doesn't push notifications.

```ts
fetch: async (url, init) => {
  const method = (init?.method || 'GET').toUpperCase()

  if (method === 'GET') {
    return new Response(null, { status: 405, statusText: 'Method Not Allowed' })
  }

  const token = await waitForToken()
  if (!token) return fetch(url, init) // let the server reject it

  const headers = new Headers(init?.headers)
  headers.set('authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
  return fetch(url, { ...init, headers })
}
```

Also adds tests covering the loop, the 405 short-circuit, the synthetic 401 case, and the recommended non-throwing pattern.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## ELI5

When your MCP Server needs a login token but doesn't have one yet, the Mastra SDK can get stuck in an endless loop trying to connect every second. ### Documentation

Added a new "Handling auth failures inside custom fetch" section to the MCPClient reference that explains the issue and provides the solution:

- **Problem**: Throwing from a custom `fetch` when authentication is unavailable triggers an indefinite ~1Hz retry loop on the SDK's background `GET /mcp` "standalone listener" stream that receives server-pushed notifications
- **Solution**: Return a synthetic `405 Method Not Allowed` Response instead, which aligns with the MCP Streamable HTTP specification and signals cleanly to the SDK to stop retrying
- **Recommended pattern**: Demonstrates a practical implementation that:
  - Waits for an auth token on POST requests with a configurable timeout
  - Short-circuits the GET listener with a synthetic 405 when the server doesn't push notifications
  - Attaches the Authorization header to outgoing requests once the token is available
  - Never throws from the custom fetch function

## Description

Fixes a regression in Mastra Studio where API errors during an agent chat (e.g. an invalid OpenAI API key) were silently swallowed in the chat UI. The error chunk was reaching the client and `toUIMessage` was correctly producing a message with `metadata.status === 'error'`, but `useChat`'s `initialMessages` `useEffect` then unconditionally replaced the local `messages` state with the (server-persisted) `initialMessages` after the stream finished — wiping the in-memory error message before the user ever saw it.

The fix is contained to `packages/playground/src/services/mastra-runtime-provider.tsx`:

- Track stream errors in a parallel `streamErrors: MastraUIMessage[]` state in `MastraRuntimeProvider`. This state survives the post-stream `initialMessages` refresh.
- Reset `streamErrors` on `agentId`/`threadId` change and at the start of every `onNew` send so errors don't leak across conversations or turns.
- Capture `chunk.type === 'error'` in both the stream and network `onChunk` callbacks, and route thrown errors from the existing `catch` block into `streamErrors` (instead of `setMessages`, which gets wiped).
- When building `vnextmessages`, strip any transient `metadata.status === 'error'` messages from `useChat`'s `messages` and append `streamErrors` instead — this avoids briefly rendering duplicate errors during the streaming window.

Existing rendering already handled the error UI: `error-aware-text.tsx` renders any message with `metadata?.status === 'error'` as a red `Notice`, and `toAssistantUIMessage` already passes the `status` through. Nothing about the rendering pipeline changed.

2. Set a fake `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-test-...` in `.env`.
3. Open Studio, send a message in the agent chat.

title: fix(playground): allow prompt block version switch to update editor and sidebar
body:
## Description

In Studio's CMS Prompt Blocks edit page (`/cms/prompts/:id/edit`), picking an older version from the version dropdown showed the "This is a previous version" notice and updated the URL with `?versionId=…`, but the editor pane and the description field in the sidebar stayed stuck on the latest version's content. A hard reload didn't help.

### Root cause

In `packages/playground/src/pages/cms/prompt-blocks/edit/index.tsx`, the form-reset effect was gated on `!form.formState.isDirty`:

```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (initialValues && !form.formState.isDirty) {
    form.reset(initialValues);
    setFormResetKey(prev => prev + 1);
  }
}, [initialValues, form]);
```

`form.formState.isDirty` becomes truthy on the very first render because `@uiw/react-codemirror` (`PromptBlockEditMain` → `Controller` → `CodeEditor`) fires `onChange` during its own initial value-sync. That call propagates through `Controller`'s `field.onChange` and dirties the form. From then on, every version switch is a no-op — `initialValues` changes when `dataSource` swaps to the selected version, but the dirty gate skips `form.reset`, so the editor + sidebar stay on the previously rendered values.

### Fix

- Drop the `!form.formState.isDirty` gate on the version-switch effect. Switching versions is an intentional user action, and `initialValues` only changes when `dataSource` (either `block` or `versionData`) changes — TanStack Query's structural sharing keeps the reference stable across no-op refetches, so this doesn't introduce spurious resets on background revalidations.
- Pipe `formResetKey` through `PromptBlockEditMain` and key the `CodeEditor` on it (mirroring the existing `JSONSchemaForm.Root` pattern in the sidebar). This forces a clean remount whenever the form is reset, which guarantees the markdown editor pane reflects the new content even if `@uiw/react-codemirror`'s internal value-sync misses an external prop change.

title: feat(server): stream live A2A resubscribe updates for in-progress tasks
body:
## Summary

This adds live in-progress `tasks/resubscribe` support for Mastra's task-first A2A server behavior.

Changes in this PR:
- return the current `Task` snapshot as the first `tasks/resubscribe` event
- continue streaming live `artifact-update` and `status-update` events for in-progress tasks
- keep terminal completion semantics through the final `status-update` event
- add focused handler coverage for terminal task snapshots, live artifact updates, and artifact-only changes

## Why

Mastra's existing `tasks/resubscribe` behavior is too thin for reconnecting clients. It only emits `status-update` events from saved task snapshots, so clients can see state changes but cannot continue receiving artifact output for an in-progress task.

This PR moves `tasks/resubscribe` to a `current snapshot + future live updates` model:
- first event: current `Task`
- future events: derived `artifact-update` and `status-update` events

This matches the ticket scope for live reconnection support without introducing historical event replay.

## Spec alignment

This is aligned with the A2A spec direction:
- A2A v0.3.0 leaves missed-event backfill implementation-defined for `tasks/resubscribe`
- the latest spec text is clearer that subscribe should start with the current `Task` and then stream task updates

References:
- v0.3.0: https://a2a-protocol.org/v0.3.0/specification/
- latest spec: https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/specification.md

## Validation

- `pnpm --filter ./packages/server exec vitest run src/server/handlers/a2a.test.ts`

Closes COR-891.

title: fix(server): bypass ownership checks when auth is not configured
body:
## Problem

When a user creates agents/skills with auth enabled (records get an `authorId`), then later disables auth, the server-side ownership checks (`assertReadAccess`, `assertWriteAccess`, `assertExecuteAccess`, `assertShareAccess`) reject requests with 404 because:

1. The record has a non-null `authorId` (set when auth was on)
2. `getCallerAuthorId()` returns `null` (no auth = no identity)
3. The old check `callerAuthorId && callerAuthorId === owner` was `false`
4. No scoped permissions exist → throws 404

## Fix

All 4 assert functions in `authorship.ts` now check for the absence of `MASTRA_USER_KEY` on the request context:

```ts
if (!callerAuthorId && !requestContext.get(MASTRA_USER_KEY)) return;
```

This is safe because when auth IS configured, `coreAuthMiddleware` rejects unauthenticated requests with 401 before they reach handlers. An absent `MASTRA_USER_KEY` at handler level genuinely means no auth provider is configured (single-user/dev mode).

### Edge cases

| Scenario | `MASTRA_USER_KEY` | `callerAuthorId` | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| No auth configured | absent | `null` | **Allow** (early return) |
| Auth configured, user has ID | present | `"user-123"` | Check ownership normally |
| Auth configured, user missing ID (misconfiguration) | present | `null` | **Reject** (falls through to 404) |

## Tests

4 new tests in `authorship.test.ts` (60 → 64), one per assert function, verifying that owned private records are accessible when no caller identity exists.

## Test plan

- `pnpm --filter ./packages/server exec vitest run src/server/handlers/authorship.test.ts` — 64/64 ✅
- `pnpm --filter ./packages/server exec tsc --noEmit` — clean

title: fix(convex): serialize workflow snapshot before insert to avoid $-prefixed key rejection
body:
Fixes #16110.

`@mastra/convex` `persistWorkflowSnapshot` was inserting the snapshot as a raw nested object. Convex reserves field names starting with `$`, and Mastra workflow snapshots embed tool outputs whose serialized Zod-to-JSON-Schema fragments contain `$schema` / `$ref` / `$defs` / `$id`. The result: every agent run with at least one Zod-schema tool crashed on the first persisted turn of the internal `agentic-loop` workflow with `ArgumentValidationError: Object contains extra field $schema that is not in the validator`.

`loadWorkflowSnapshot` already accepts a string-encoded snapshot, so the fix is symmetric — stringify on the way in.

```ts
// before
record: { ..., snapshot, ... }

// after
record: { ..., snapshot: JSON.stringify(snapshot), ... }
```

Added a unit test in `stores/convex/src/storage/domains/workflows/workflows.test.ts` that constructs a snapshot with `$`-prefixed keys, mocks the Convex client, and asserts no `$`-keyed object reaches the inserted record. Test fails on `main`, passes with the fix.

title: fix(playground): prevent IME composition Enter from submitting agent …
body:
…chat

When using a Chinese/Japanese/Korean IME to input text, pressing Enter to confirm character selection was triggering the chat form submission instead of completing the IME composition.

Root cause: ComposerPrimitive.Input uses Radix's asChild Slot pattern which merges the primitive's internal onKeyDown (which submits on Enter) with the textarea's handlers. IME composition events fire before the keydown, but without checking isComposing the Enter key always submits.

Fix: Add an isComposingRef (useRef) and wire onCompositionStart/End to flip the flag. In onKeyDown, stop propagation when Enter fires during an active IME composition so the primitive never sees it as a submit.

Fixes #16109

## Description

When using a Chinese/Japanese/Korean IME to input text in the Agent Chat
interface, pressing **Enter** to confirm character selection was triggering
form submission instead of completing the IME composition cycle.

This regression was introduced in v1.7.1 (background task feature, #15307)
which added `onChange={e => setThreadInput?.(e.target.value)}` to the
`<textarea asChild>` inside `ComposerPrimitive.Input`.

**Root cause:**

`ComposerPrimitive.Input` uses Radix's `asChild` / `Slot` pattern, which
merges the primitive's internal `onKeyDown` (Enter → submit) with the
textarea's handlers.  IME composition fires `compositionstart` /
`compositionend` events around character selection, but without a
`isComposing` guard the primitive's Enter handler fires unconditionally,
submitting the message mid-composition.

title: Optimize listTraces and listBranches on DuckDB
body:
Extracted from larger PR: https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/15747

## Description

Significantly improves `listTraces` and `listBranches` query performance on DuckDB by introducing a two-stage filtering strategy. Both methods previously rebuilt every span in `span_events` (or every branch-typed span) before applying filters, ordering, and pagination. They now narrow on raw rows first and only reconstruct the spans that actually need to be returned.

1. **Prefilter stage**: Filters raw `span_events` start rows using scalar columns (entity*, *Id, service, environment, startedAt range, etc.) before any span reconstruction. `listTraces` adds `parentSpanId IS NULL`; `listBranches` adds `spanType IN (BRANCH_SPAN_TYPES)` (or the caller's narrower `spanType` if supplied).

2. **Post-aggregation stage**: Reconstructs spans only for prefilter candidates, then applies filters that depend on reconstructed values (status, tags, metadata, scope, endedAt range, and `hasChildError` on `listTraces`).

When no post-aggregation filters are present, ordering and pagination happen inside the prefilter CTE, so reconstruction touches at most `perPage` rows rather than the full filtered set.

The `hasChildError` filter on `listTraces` now runs directly against raw `span_events` instead of the reconstructed-spans CTE, eliminating unnecessary reconstruction overhead.

**API compatibility**: Public return shapes (`SpanRecord` / `ListTracesResponse` / `ListBranchesResponse`) and filter semantics are unchanged; this is purely an internal optimization.

## Related Issue(s)

Extracted from #15747.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [x] Performance improvement
- [x] Test update

## Changes

- Added `parseFieldKey` import from `@mastra/core/utils` for safe ORDER BY field handling on raw events.
- Introduced `PREFILTER_KEYS` defining the scalar columns that can be safely pushed down to the prefilter stage.
- Added `partitionAnchorFilters()` to split filters into `prefilter` / `postAgg` / `hasChildError` buckets. Reused by both `listTraces` and `listBranches`.
- Updated `buildHasChildErrorClause()` to take a `rootAlias` parameter and run `EXISTS` against raw `span_events` rather than the reconstructed-spans CTE.
- Refactored `listTraces()` into a fast path / slow path:
  - **Fast path** (no post-agg filters, not ordering by `endedAt`): order and paginate on raw start rows, reconstruct only the page.
  - **Slow path**: narrow to candidate roots first, reconstruct just those, then apply post-agg `WHERE`.
- Refactored `listBranches()` with the same two-stage strategy. The existing `spanType IN (BRANCH_SPAN_TYPES)` guard is preserved and combined with the scalar prefilter; non-branch `spanType` inputs still short-circuit to an empty result.
- Mapped `startedAt` ordering to the start-row `timestamp` for prefilter-side sorts; tightened sort-direction validation. Added the `endedAt.end` upper-bound trick on the prefilter timestamp to avoid scanning events that started after the requested window.
- Added Vitest cases covering scalar prefilter (fast path) + tag post-filter (slow path) for both `listTraces` and `listBranches`.

- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

## Overview

Implements a two-stage filtering strategy in the DuckDB observability store to dramatically reduce span reconstruction work for listTraces and listBranches: a scalar prefilter against raw span_events start rows, followed by post-aggregation filters applied only to reconstructed candidates. When safe, a fast-path performs ordering and pagination inside the prefilter so at most perPage spans are reconstructed; otherwise a slow path reconstructs candidates then post-filters.

- Two-stage filtering:
  - Prefilter: pushable scalar predicates on raw span_events start rows (PREFILTER_KEYS: entity*, *Id, service, environment, startedAt range, etc.). listTraces also requires parentSpanId IS NULL; listBranches restricts to BRANCH_SPAN_TYPES (and short-circuits to empty for non-branch requests).

title: perf(convex): batch bulk storage mutations
body:
Closes #16147.

This PR removes the serial await waterfall from Convex storage bulk mutations by batching independent lookup, insert, patch, and delete work in bounded chunks of 25. It applies the same behavior across typed tables, vector tables, and the generic fallback table, while preserving the existing clear/drop page size and `hasMore` behavior.

`deleteMany` now deduplicates ids before indexed lookup. `batchInsert` now coalesces duplicate records before writing: typed tables merge duplicate records by id to preserve the previous sequential patch behavior, while vector and generic fallback tables keep the last duplicate because those paths replace the stored payload.

The local benchmark compared compiled baseline `HEAD` against the compiled optimized branch using the actual storage handler and a mocked Convex ctx with 5ms latency per DB read/write. This is a focused local latency benchmark, not a production Convex deployment benchmark.

| Path | Baseline avg | Optimized avg | Change | Concurrency |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `deleteMany` with 100 ids | 1024.4ms | 41.2ms | ~24.9x faster | reads/writes `1 -> 25` |
| `batchInsert` with 100 records | 1023.5ms | 41.4ms | ~24.7x faster | reads/writes `1 -> 25` |
| `clearTable` with 100 docs available | 133.0ms | 10.3ms | ~12.9x faster | deletes `1 -> 25` |

Single-item bulk calls were also checked against the same benchmark setup and did not show a measurable slowdown: `deleteMany` stayed at 10.3ms, `batchInsert` moved from 10.2ms to 10.3ms, and `clearTable` stayed at 10.2ms.

Verified with `pnpm --filter ./stores/convex exec vitest run src/server/storage.test.ts`, `pnpm --filter ./stores/convex test`, `pnpm --filter ./stores/convex lint`, `pnpm --filter ./stores/convex build:lib`, and `git diff --check`.

title: fix(memory): skip async reflection buffering when observation tokens are below activation point
body:
## Description

When idle timeout (`activateAfterIdle`) or provider-change triggers fire in `maybeReflect`, the TTL/provider-change check at line 821 bypasses the reflection threshold gate (correctly — these triggers should activate *existing* buffered reflections regardless of token count). However, when `tryActivateBufferedReflection` finds no buffered reflection to activate and `blockAfter` isn't exceeded, the code falls through to `startAsyncBufferedReflection` **without checking whether observation tokens meet the activation point** (`reflectThreshold × bufferActivation`).

This causes unnecessary background reflection operations with very few observation tokens — e.g. 0.5k tokens against a 10k activation point (50% of 20k max).

**Fix:** Add an activation point check (`observationTokens < reflectThreshold * bufferActivation`) before starting a new async buffered reflection in the TTL/provider-change fallback path. This does not affect the normal threshold-triggered path (where `observationTokens >= reflectThreshold > activationPoint`), nor does it affect activation of already-buffered reflections.

**Tests added:**
- TTL trigger with tokens below activation point → no async reflection started
- Provider-change trigger with tokens below activation point → no async reflection started
- TTL trigger with tokens above activation point → async reflection correctly started (positive case)
